_comment: C0 body translation · lakera-ai (2026-11-06). Key contract per cursor.en.json; sources/related counts must match the source file.

axes.model_access: What it guards and evaluates is not one vendor's model but your application chain: the docs list Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Salesforce Agentforce, n8n, Relevance AI and MCP servers as integration surfaces. The Guard API takes text (a POST with messages and project_id), not weights; whether the underlying detection model can be swapped or a tier chosen: not disclosed officially — the API Reference only exposes git_revision and model_version inside the response's developer info.
axes.runtime: Delivered from the cloud: sign-up and configuration at platform.lakera.ai, detection through the hosted API at api.lakera.ai, authentication of the form "Authorization: Bearer $LAKERA_GUARD_API_KEY", and the official quickstart call is POST https://api.lakera.ai/v2/guard. The site self-describes as "The AI-Native Security Platform", with product lines Workforce AI Security, AI Agent Security and AI Red Teaming. A local or private-deployment form: no official statement captured in this pass, recorded as unknown.
axes.local_files: Nothing lands locally: prompts and responses are sent and returned by your application, and decisions can be reviewed in the console's Guard results surface (the docs list the /guard and /guard/results endpoints). Export format, retention duration and deletion path for hit records: not given item by item on the pages on record, moved to unknowns.
axes.background: Two kinds of asynchronous behaviour must be read separately: Guard is a synchronous API call that the official framing describes as real-time screening; Red is a hosted assessment project, documented as four steps (enumeration, attack development, impact testing, reporting) delivering "detailed findings with remediation guidance". Project duration, concurrency limits and result notification: not stated officially.
axes.tools: Two API endpoints on record (/guard and /guard/results), with a boolean flagged verdict in the response. The integration surface is the list in the model_access axis, where "MCP servers" appears among the protected objects — meaning it both acts as MCP-side protection and treats MCP servers as objects under inspection. Concrete transports and tool-approval semantics: not verified item by item in this pass.
axes.context: Verdicts are organised per text request, and policies are tiered per project (Project mode decides between "block the interaction or logging for investigation"), so its "memory" surface is project and policy configuration, not cross-session context. Cross-session memory or history stitching: not stated officially, recorded as unknown.
axes.permissions: Read clause by clause from the official terms: the privacy entry 301s to checkpoint.com/privacy, where the entity is written as "Check Point Software Technologies Ltd."; the retention sentence reads "We will retain your information for as long as necessary to achieve the purposes described in this Privacy Policy."; the transfer sentence reads "We may collect and transfer Personal Data on a global basis", with transfers outside the EEA/UK handled via adequacy or one of the other listed mechanisms; the usage sentence includes "We may use telemetry, threat indicators … including capabilities powered by artificial intelligence (AI)". ⚠ Those sentences speak about personal data and telemetry, and **do not separately address retention or training use of customer prompt content** — that item goes to unknowns, with no inference. Commercial tiers: the pricing entry redirects to platform.lakera.ai/pricing, which did not render tier text when fetched; this site does not collect prices.
axes.fit: Fits: needing live control of prompt injection / jailbreak / PII leakage / violating content inside the request path, accepting that detection runs vendor-side; needing policies that switch per project between blocking and logging only; already running Bedrock, Copilot Studio, Agentforce, n8n or MCP servers. Not a fit: mandatory offline or private deployment (no such statement captured); wanting to swap or choose the underlying detection model; wanting only a reproducible self-run scan for engineering evidence (that is the garak and PyRIT direction); and Red assessments are not self-serve.

runs:
**This site has not run it end to end**: no /guard call issued, no Red assessment project run, so no latency, accuracy or ratio conclusions and no product rankings. This archive only organises statements on record at the official site, the redirect evidence, Check Point's privacy policy, four docs pages and the changelog.

**Suggested measurements** (four):

- **What "logging" actually returns**: when Project mode is set to log-only, what shape of response your application receives (the flagged field and downstream handling)
- **Traceability of model_version in responses**: whether it is usable for change audit, which the vendor does not state
- **Retention and deletion path for customer prompt content** (the terms do not separate it; see unknowns)
- **Whether a private/on-prem form exists** (no official statement captured)
unknowns:
- Retention period, deletion path and training use of customer prompt/response content (the terms do not address it separately)
- Compliance certificates and audit material (SOC 2, ISO 27001, DPA, subprocessor list): not named on the pages captured
- Whether a private or self-hosted form exists
- Commercial tier structure and quotas (the pricing redirect did not render tier text)
- Whether the underlying detection model can be replaced or chosen
- The concrete MCP integration transport and tool-approval semantics
- Red assessment turnaround, concurrency and deliverable format
- Mainland-network direct reachability and filing status (not measured, not searched)
related: Also a hosted content-safety API: that archive sits under Azure's account and region terms, this one under the Check Point entity's SaaS terms.
Two ends of the same question: this archive is a hosted verdict inside the request path, that one is a red-teaming pipeline you orchestrate and record yourself.
One of the integration surfaces on record: an agent workflow platform is exactly the object shape it protects.
